newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Gdansk honours Bush, Walesa, Weizsaecker.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Gdansk honours Bush, Walesa, Weizsaecker.

text.p: George Bush, Lech Walesa and Richard von Weizsaecker swapped jokes and compared marriages on Monday when the three former presidents were made honorary citizens of the Polish city of Gdansk.

Gdansk, where Walesa founded Solidarity, the Soviet bloc's first free trade union, in 1980 and led it, with Western support, to victory over communism nine years later, is in party mood this year as it celebrates its millenium.
The atmosphere rubbed off on the former U.S. and German presidents when they were escorted round the city by Walesa, Poland's president until 1995.
As they waited for their wives to return from an exhibition, Bush said this was the first time in 48 years of marriage that he had waited for his wife.
When Germany's Weizsaecker said he had been married for 38 years, Walesa told them, to cries of "Well you are young then," that his marriage had lasted 33 years.
The former presidents lunched at Walesa's home, starting with a dish called "Herrings a la Walesa" composed of marinaded fish on pineapple with whipped cream.
The gathering had its serious side. The three laid flowers at the city's memorial to shipyard workers killed during food price demonstrations crushed by communist authorities in 1970.

Speeches made as at the citizenships ceremony recalled Bush's contribution as vice president and then as U.S. president to the victory of democracy in Europe and paid tribute to Weizsaecker's role in German-Polish understanding.

Both visitors praised the role of Walesa, now in opposition and taking a low political profile in the build-up to September general elections when his old Solidarity union is leading a challenge to the ruling ex-communists.
"Lech Walesa will always remain an example of courage," Weizsaecker said in his speech at Gdansk's old city hall.
